question: Arun was performing an experiment in the laboratory. He took a solution of ferric chloride and added some smaller pieces of zinc. When the yellow colour of ferric chloride disappeared, which compound was formed?
solution:
The correct answer is **ZnCl₂.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ZnCl₂**

 
 
• The chemical compound **zinc chloride** has the formula ZnCl2.
 
• At this time, **nine distinct crystalline** forms of zinc chloride are known. The color of these ZnCl2 hydrates can be white or colorless. They are all highly water-soluble.
 
• Zinc chloride has hygroscopic properties, which means that it **draws in and holds water molecules** from the environment. As a result, protecting zinc chloride from moisture is crucial.
 
• **ZnCl₂(H₂O)****ₙ**, where n can be 1, 1.5, 2.5, 3, or 4, is the general formula for the five known** hydrates **of zinc chloride.
 
• Solid ZnCl₂ can have any one of the following crystal structures due to its polymorphism: **orthorhombic, monoclinic, and tetragonal.**
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction**
 
 
• A displacement reaction occurs when **one or more atoms** in a molecule are displaced by another atom. For instance, when iron is added to a solution containing copper sulfate, the **copper metal is displaced.**
 
• **Chlorine** takes the place of bromine in the sodium bromide solution when it is added as a gas or as a gas dissolved in water.
 
• Chlorine replaces sodium bromide with bromine, causing the solutions to turn blue because **chlorine is more reactive than bromine.**
 
• The displaced bromine is the **brown color.** The equation shows that the Cl and Br have moved from their original positions.
 
• Reaction: **Cl₂(aq) + 2NaBr(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + Br₂(aq)​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fe (OH)**3

 
 
• The chemical compound with the formula Fe(OH)₃ is iron (III) hydroxide, which is made from **hydrogen, iron, and oxygen.**
 
• The color of iron III hydroxides ranges from **dark brown to black **depending on how hydrated they are, how big and how small the particles are, and how they are shaped.
 
 
 
• **FeCl2****​**
 
 
• Ferric chloride is a crystal with a **dark color **and an iron oxidation state of +3.** Molysite** and Iron (III) chloride are other names for it.
 
• **Molysite** solution has a **faint odor **of hydrochloric acid (HCl) and is colorless to light brown. It damages most** tissues and metals.**
 
• It is widely used for **sewage treatment **and water purification because it is not flammable.
 
 
 
• **Zn (OH)**2​
 
 
• Zn (OH)₂ is the chemical formula for the inorganic compound zinc hydroxide. It naturally occurs in **wulfingite, ashoverite, and sweetite**, three rare minerals.
 
• It is a hydroxide that is **amphoteric**. Both bases and acids react with zinc hydroxide. It dissolves in strong acid because it is an **insoluble hydroxide.**
